questions.q: What opens the Edit Tooltip dialog box?
options: Opening the Extract dialog
Right-clicking the workbook title
Double-clicking the Data pane
Clicking Tooltip on the Marks card
questions.explain: The Tooltip button on the Marks card opens the Edit Tooltip dialog, where you can add, remove, and format the text and fields shown on hover.

questions.q: By default, how does Tableau populate a new tooltip?
options: It only shows the sheet's title
It copies the tooltip from a different, unrelated worksheet
It auto-fills placeholders for every field currently in the view
It leaves the tooltip completely blank
questions.explain: Tableau automatically inserts a placeholder for every field on the shelves and Marks card, which you can then edit, remove, or reformat.

options: A setting that disables tooltips entirely
A type of calculated field
A way to export a tooltip as an image file
A feature that embeds an entire second worksheet inside the tooltip of a mark
questions.explain: Viz in Tooltip lets you insert a fully separate worksheet so that hovering over a mark reveals a complete secondary chart, not just text.

questions.q: How do labels differ from tooltips?
options: Labels only work with map visualizations
They are the exact same feature with two different names
Labels are always-on text baked directly onto marks; tooltips only appear on hover
Labels only appear on hover; tooltips are always visible
questions.explain: Labels are permanently visible text attached to marks, while tooltips are hidden until the user hovers over a mark.

questions.q: In the Viz in Tooltip example from this lesson, what does hovering over the Office Supplies bar reveal?
options: A full breakdown by sub-category, each with its own mini bar and dollar value
The underlying SQL query
A blank tooltip with no data
A pop-up asking you to connect to a new data source
questions.explain: The embedded second worksheet renders a sub-category breakdown for Office Supplies directly inside the tooltip when you hover over that bar.
